chapters.summary: Rabbi Mendelson of Congregation Machane Chodosh delivers an invocation reflecting on October 7th, his great-grandfather's activism, and the sanctity of life, asking for wisdom and compassion in deliberations.
chapters.title: Invocation by Rabbi Yossi Mendelson

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: We will now have today's invocation, which will be delivered by Rabbi Yossi Mendelsohn of Congregation Mahanei Hadosh, which is located at 11012 68th Avenue in Queens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: There are moments in life that force us to face what matters most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: In times of crisis, we have to choose between the superficial and the authentic, between the temporal and the eternal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: October 7th, 2023 was one such day for me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: It was a holy day, and my religious observances limited my access to accurate information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And so in that fog of uncertainty, my imagination ran wild with a terrible possibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: What, if never again, turned out to be a false hope?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And I thought of my great, great, great grandfather, Abraham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: My great-grandfather, Abraham Baroff, came to this country, escaping violence against Jews at the end of the 19th century, and he became the patriarch of seven generations of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: He thought he'd survive as a poet and journalist, but when he saw the crisis of disadvantaged workers, he stepped up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Leading the Garment Workers Union as they desperately tried to prevent tragedies like the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: His life reminds me that never again is not just about survival.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Instead, it's about what you stand for.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: It's about what survives through you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: His fight for justice, fairness, and humanity continued the life and teaching of his great forefather, his namesake, the biblical Abraham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: The biblical Abraham's message is this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: As life is everywhere, so too its source.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: The source of life is known by many names, but really is beyond any name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: The infinite, eternal, and almighty is beyond gender and class.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: We are all contained and sustained by the same source.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: God is bigger than religion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: There is no place, no aspect of life where the Almighty is absent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And I believe that the biblical Abraham would see what's happening right here

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: right now in this august chambers as the fulfillment of his message.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Look, women and men whose decisions will shape the future of this great city and in many ways guide the course of the whole world are beginning their deliberations and their work with a moment of sincere reflection and prayer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: God is here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Even in the halls of human power, we invite a reminder of our sacred responsibility to humanity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: That we remember to care for each other as the source of life cares for us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: That we remember our obligation to uphold the dignity of every human life,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: to strengthen the families and communities that sustain life, and to craft policies grounded in compassion, responsibility, and the sanctity of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Never again begins in remembrance, deepens through prayer, but must live through action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: In the choices we make, the institutions we build, and the lives we refuse to abandon,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And so, let us pray.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: May the one source of life, Almighty God, guide our deliberations and our decisions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: May we act with wisdom and compassion, humility and courage.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: May we affirm the dignity of every human life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And nurture the families and communities through which life flourishes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: And may the favor and pleasantness of the all-merciful and almighty rest on our work for peace and prosperity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rabbi Yossi Mendelson
utterances.text: Amen.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Rabbi Mendelsohn.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: I would now ask Council Member Lynn Shulman to spread the invocation on the record.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Rabbi Yosef Mendelsohn has served for 16 years as the spiritual leader of Congregation Mahani Hodish in Forest Hills, Queens, a synagogue widely known for its warm, inclusive, and uplifting atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Over his many years of leadership, he has built deep roots in a broad network of connections across the rich and diverse communities of Queens.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: A dedicated educator with over two decades of teaching experience, he also serves as the local representative for the Roy Jewish Learning Institute, making high-level Jewish learning accessible to adults of all backgrounds.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: A graduate of the Rabbinical College of Canada, Rabbi Mendelsohn provides spiritual care to individuals of all faiths as a chaplain at New York Presbyterian Queens Hospital, where he serves on both the clinical, pastoral, training faculty, and the ethics committee.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: He previously chaired the Bible Studies Department at the Jewish Institute of Queens and is an active member of the Rabbinical Council of Queens.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: He and his wife, Mushki, who is here today, are the proud parents of seven children and have one son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I now make a motion to spread the invocation in full upon the record.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin discusses Monday's committee of the whole oversight hearing on artificial intelligence, thanking members, noting whistleblower testimony, and arguing for responsible guardrails and legislation in the absence of federal regulation.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Recaps AI Oversight Hearing and Proposed Legislation

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: We will now have communication from Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This week has certainly been no ordinary week.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And Monday's hearing was no ordinary hearing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We convened a rare committee of the whole oversight hearing to discuss artificial intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I first of all want to thank all the members who attended.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It was just an incredible, incredible hearing.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And many of you stuck it out along with myself and Chair De La Rosa to the bitter, bitter end late at night.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so really appreciated that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We discussed the benefits it may produce, the threats it may pose, and the responsible guardrails around it that we have proposed to ensure that New Yorkers are protected.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We listened to incredibly compelling testimony from whistleblowers that had come from all over the country, from experts, from academics.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We heard from city agencies to receive their perspectives on the policy.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: that we are seeking to implement.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And we asked questions to the firms leading the research and development of this very technology.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: One thing was very clear.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Their answers were concerningly insufficient and hardly instilled confidence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We are proud to be the city, let me be clear, with the most tech jobs in the country, even more than San Francisco, over 400,000 jobs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We're so thrilled to be able to have all of these different startups that are locating here, that are doing incredible work in AI around medical and scientific breakthroughs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We do not want to stifle innovation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On the contrary, we want to foster it.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And the best way to continue that responsible growth of AI is to ensure that New Yorkers have faith and confidence that the models that the frontier AI companies are releasing are indeed safe.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So if it is, quote unquote, it is more likely than not that we would lose control to AIs and it could end in human extinction, this is a direct quote that whistleblower Jacob Coxon told us on Monday,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: then companies self-regulating this industry is one solution.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That accelerates that and that really can cause concern.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So this certainly doesn't have to be the case.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It's in our power to ensure that it isn't.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And I'm certainly hopeful that our hearing can serve as a model for meaningful progress at the state, excuse me, or federal.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And let me just say one other word on that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Obviously, we want to see action on the federal level, as I said on Monday, but there has not been that.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And so in the absence of federal regulation, it is absolutely...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our obligation in New York City to step up when all of these companies have huge outposts here employing thousands and thousands of workers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And as I said at the hearing, just like the pharmaceutical industry doesn't self-regulate, you of course have the FDA.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Just as the airline industry doesn't self-regulate, you have the FAA.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Just like the financial services firms don't self-regulate, they have the SEC and other agencies.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So similarly,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Our legislation, and I want to thank the colleagues who introduced legislation, that package of bills, those 10 bills, are really important to ensure responsible development of safe models moving forward.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And as I said, I look forward to having other committees have hearings on AI and consider additional legislation as well.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So Monday was the beginning of that.

chapters.summary: She announces the expansion of a pilot program that expedites funding to not-for-profits to 30 days, now benefiting over 800 organizations and cutting payment timelines by 300%.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Announces Expansion of Nonprofit Funding Pilot

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This morning, I was proud to make an announcement along with a number of colleagues here and the mayor that the council is expanding

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: a pilot program that expedites the distribution of funding to not-for-profit so that they can receive it in 30 days.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, right?

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: It matters.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: successfully cutting payment timelines by around 300% on average.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Together with the mayoral administration, this initial discretionary grant pilot had originally last year served 100 not-for-profits.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Now we're doing an expansion to benefit over 800 not-for-profits.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That are working on the ground to improve the lives of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Specifically, the streamlined process eliminates over half a dozen steps of the bureaucratic odyssey that previously burdened not-for-profits.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: So we look forward to making it easier for more not-for-profits to access the funding that they were promised in order to help keeping the people of our city.

chapters.summary: She announces funding for panic buttons and security cameras for small businesses, building on efforts with Attorney General Tish James to curb retail theft.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Announces Security Funding for Small Businesses

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Speaking of essential assistance, today we also announced that we're furthering support for small businesses through funding that will be used to install panic buttons and security cameras for small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: This is building on joint efforts of both the council and Attorney General Tish James to curb retail theft because employees must be safe and feel safe when they are at work.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: As the city develops a permanent security program for small retail businesses under Local Law 120, this initiative comes in advance of its implementation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Certainly protecting public safety and strengthening economic vibrancy come hand in hand, and we are so excited to make progress on both of those priorities.

chapters.summary: She marks three years since the October 7th attack, remembers the 1,200 lives lost, and shares meeting with Nova Festival survivor Shalev Betan and Yunus Al-Kanwari.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Commemorates October 7th Anniversary

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Yesterday marked three years since October 7th, the worst day in Israel's history and the deadliest attack on the Jewish state since its founding.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Jews across the world remember the terror of that morning.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They recalled the fear and the hatred it stoked, and we mourned the innocent, unfulfilled lives that were lost that way.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Over 1,200 lives that were lost by Hamas terrorists.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A few weeks ago, I was honored to meet with Nova Festival survivor Shalev Betan, as well as Yunus Al-Kanwari, the man who hid Shalev and his friends on his farm, saving dozens of lives.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: They shared their truly remarkable stories, and may we continue to take in their message of showing compassion to all.

chapters.summary: Speaker Menin notes the Council's celebration of Italian Heritage Month with hundreds of Italian Americans, performances, proclamations, and food.
chapters.title: Council Celebrates Italian Heritage Month

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On a lighter note, last night the Council celebrated Italian Heritage Month in the chambers with hundreds of Italian Americans.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Italian American community comprises about 10% of our city,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: and we're incredibly grateful for their countless contributions, which we commemorated with performances, proclamations, and plenty of pane alavaca.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And this weekend continues with Columbus Day celebrations.

chapters.summary: She acknowledges the upcoming Indigenous Peoples Day, the history of the Lenape people, and the nearly 200,000 indigenous people living in NYC.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Recognizes Indigenous Peoples Day

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: On Monday, we will also celebrate Indigenous Peoples Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We acknowledge our city's rich past, including the history of the Lenape people, who are thought to have migrated here about 3,000 years ago.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, there are almost 200,000 indigenous people living in New York City, the largest single concentration of Native people in the country, and we will continue to uplift these communities.

chapters.summary: She recognizes World Teachers Day, noting nearly 100,000 public school teachers shaping 800,000 students.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Honors World Teachers Day

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: October 5th, it was World Teachers Day.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Education heightens our children's potential, giving them the foundation they need to succeed.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have almost 100,000 public school teachers in our city shaping the lives of 800,000 students, and the work that they do each and every day is truly invaluable.

chapters.summary: She highlights Domestic Violence Awareness Month, noting nearly 40% of felony assaults were domestic violence last year, and expresses support for survivors.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Marks Domestic Violence Awareness Month

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: October is National Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Domestic violence is a central...

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: But under-recognized driver of serious crimes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Last year, nearly 40% of felony assaults were classified as domestic violence.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: To make our city safer, we have to focus on reducing crime that happens behind closed doors.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: To our survivors, we see you and we support you.

chapters.summary: She welcomes students from the Student Voice NYC Citywide Leadership Team and their mentor Lynette Townsley, listing participating schools and districts.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Welcomes Student Voice NYC Leadership Team

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Finally, I'd like to welcome some students from the Student Voice NYC Citywide Leadership Team.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And they're, yes.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And their mentor, Lynette Townsley.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Lynette.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The Queens Community Board 12 Youth Committee Chair.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: These youth have come from all over our city to see the lawmaking process for themselves.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: We have students here from Eagle Academy for Young Men of Southeast Queens and Deputy Speaker Williams District.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: PS 48Q and Life Camp and Councilmember Ty Hankerson's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: PS 95Q in Councilmember Linda Lee's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Path Performing Arts and Technology High School in Councilmember Chris Banks'district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And Bronx School for Law, Government, and Justice and Councilmember Althea Stevens District.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Welcome to the People's House.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Okay, thank you so much for joining us.

chapters.summary: She lists several land use items including Sojourner Truth MAPS rezoning, 158-06 Northern Boulevard, 69-67 108th Street, 21-31 46th Avenue, 132 Melrose Street, Fort Hamilton Mews, Park Avenue Brooklyn, and 289 Kent Avenue, noting modifications for deeper affordability.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Outlines Land Use Items for Vote

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Now we are going to move on to our stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: First, we'll vote on the following land use items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Sojourn or Truth MAPS rezoning will facilitate the development of two new 100% affordable residential mixed-use buildings ranging in height from 6 to 16 stories with 457 housing units.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: And 15,000 square feet of community facility space in Councilmember Oswald Velez's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 158-06 Northern Boulevard rezoning will facilitate the development of new nine-story mixed-use development with approximately 76 dwelling units,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 19 of which will be permanently affordable, pursuant to MIH Option 1, and retail space in Councilmember Sandra Ong's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council is modifying this application to remove a portion of the rezoning area not owned by the applicant.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 69-67 108th Street rezoning will facilitate the development of a new

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 11-story mixed-use building with approximately 59 residential units, up to 15 of which will be permanently affordable in Councilmember Lynn Shulman's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council is modifying this application to strike MIH option 2 and add MIH option 3, which will ensure deeper affordability.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 21-3146 Avenue rezoning will facilitate the development of a new

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 11-story mixed-use building with approximately 70 residential units, up to 18 of which will be permanently affordable, as well as ground floor community facility or commercial space in Councilmember Julie Wan's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council's modifying this application to strike MIH option 2 and add MIH option 3, which will ensure deeper affordability.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 132 Melrose Street rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Will facilitate the development of a six-story mixed-use residential and commercial building with 18 dwelling units, five of which will be income-restricted, pursuant to MIH Option 1 in Councilmember Jennifer Gutierrez's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council's modifying this application to strike MIH Option 2.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Fort Hamilton Mews rezoning will facilitate the development of 11-story mixed-use building with 292 residential units,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: up to 88 of which will be permanently affordable, pursuant to MIH, as well as 200 parking spaces and commercial community facility space in Councilmember Kayla Santasoso's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council's modifying the application from an RZX district to an RZD district and to add MIH option one.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Two applications in Councilmember Lincoln-Ressler's district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Park Avenue Brooklyn rezoning will facilitate 10 new developments, including four education institutions serving 2,500 students and six schools.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: mixed-use residential buildings with 391 units, 91-117 of which will be permanently income-restricted.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: 289 Kent Avenue Resoning will facilitate the development of one new 18-story mixed-use building.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: With 278 dwelling units, approximately 70 of which will be permanently income restricted.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Council is modifying both of these applications to strike MIH option 2, add MIH option 3, which will ensure deeper affordability.

chapters.summary: She describes two pre-considered resolutions sponsored by Council Member Linda Lee establishing 40-year Article 11 tax exemptions for buildings in several districts.
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Outlines Finance Items for Vote

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Next, we're going to vote on the following finance items.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: A pre-considered resolution sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee would establish a full 40-year Article 11 tax exemption for two buildings in the districts of Councilmember Eric Genowitz and Oswald Philez.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Pre-considered resolution sponsored by Councilmember Linda Lee.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Would establish a 40-year Article 11 tax exemption for one building in Councilmember Shahan Hanif's district.

chapters.summary: She lists resolutions and introductions: Res 458 (Little Yemen cultural district), Res 646 (Hindu American Awareness Month), Intro 489A (towing database), Intro 684 (gifted and talented access study), Res 328 (tax credit for construction-affected businesses), and Intro 799 (loans for construction-affected small businesses).
chapters.title: Speaker Menin Outlines Legislation for Vote

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Today, we'll also vote on the following pieces of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 458, sponsored by Councilmember Shirley Aldebal, calling on the governor to sign.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: S6487C-A70333D to empower the New York State Council on the Arts to designate Little Yemen as a cultural district.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Regina Paul.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 646, sponsored by Councilmember Amanda Farias, would declare October as Hindu American Awareness and Appreciation Month in the City of New York.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you again to Regina Paul.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 489A, sponsored by Councilmember Ina Vernikoff, would require the Department of Finance to create

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: a centralized online database and notification system for vehicles towed by city entities or private tow operators.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: The bill also allows vehicle owners to opt in to notifications when their vehicle is entered into the system.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to John Kingsley and Rachel Codrero.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 684, sponsored by Councilmember Susan Zhuang, would require the Mayor's Office of Child Care and Early Childhood Education, in consultation with the Department of Education and community-based early childhood organizations,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to study how language access needs and geographic location affect preschool-age children's access

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: to early elementary gifted and talented programs.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Alejandro Carjavel.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Resolution 328, sponsored by Councilmember Yusuf Salam, would call on the New York State Legislature to pass and the Governor to sign legislation providing a tax credit to businesses negatively affected by infrastructure

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Tyler Walls and Rebecca Barilla.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Introduction 799, also sponsored by Councilmember Yusuf Salam, would require the Department of Small Business Services to establish a program to provide loans, grants, services, materials,

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: or some combination thereof to support small businesses affected by city construction projects.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you to Tyler Walls, Rebecca Barilla, and Jessica Boulet.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: Thank you for your attention to that.

chapters.summary: Krishnan takes over, notes rules for general orders, and grants a limited exception for Deputy Speaker Williams and Council Member Lee to recognize delegations, then calls on Council Member Zhuang.
chapters.title: Majority Leader Krishnan Opens General Orders Discussion

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: I'm now going to turn it over to our majority leader.

utterances.speaker: Julie Menin
utterances.text: That's what I'm calling you.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: I'm getting used to that, you know?

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Power's getting to my head slowly.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: We will now move into discussion of general orders.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Under the Council rules for general orders, members are to speak on the matters of today's stated agenda.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Today we'll make a limited exception for Council Member, Deputy Speaker Williams and Council Member Lee to recognize two honorable delegations that are here today.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: But we will begin with Council Member Zhuang, followed by Deputy Speaker Williams.

chapters.summary: Zhuang speaks in favor of Intro 684, which requires data collection on language access and geographic location affecting access to early elementary gifted and talented programs, emphasizing equity for immigrant and low-income families.
chapters.title: Council Member Zhuang Urges Support for Intro 684 on Gifted and Talented Access

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader, today.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Today, I'm asking my colleagues to support our children and families across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Intro 684, take an important step towards making every child has a fair opportunity to access gifted and talented education programs.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Specially, 684 requires us to collect the data to see where the gifted and talented program are and who have the access to them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This is important data.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: As a mom with kids in our public schools, I know how important the data is.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And I know how many families, like immigrant families, low-income families, and minority families, face barriers that can make these opportunities feel out of reach.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: This data collection helped us better understand those gaps, like how language access, location affect who learns about those programs and who get in them.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Passing Intro 684 is a critical day for access and equity for all, because we know every child deserves a fair chance.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: And every child is talented in their own way.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: We just need to make sure children in all our communities have access to every program they deserve.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: Please vote yes.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Next is Deputy Speaker Williams, followed by Councilmember Banks.

chapters.summary: Williams welcomes young people from schools across Queens, Brooklyn, and the Bronx for Youth Empowerment Day, thanking mentors and organizations.
chapters.title: Deputy Speaker Williams Welcomes Youth Empowerment Day Participants

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you, Acting Majority Leader Krishnan.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I want to give a quick shout-out to the young people who joined us today at City Hall for Youth Empowerment Day, representing schools across Queens, Brooklyn, and the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Of course, a special shout-out to Eagle Academy that is located in my district.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I want to thank Lynette Townsley, the New York State Conference of NAACP Youth Division.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I believe we have the president here alongside NCNW, BU, National Action Network, and Zeta Phi Beta Sorority Incorporated.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And thank you so much to all the young people who are here today for being engaged and taking an interest in what happens in our city.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We may have some future council members and lawmakers sitting in our audience today.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you so much for being here.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Deputy Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Now we have Councilmember Banks, followed by Councilmember Lee.

chapters.summary: Banks speaks in favor of Intro 684, arguing families should not need money or connections to access quality education, and thanks Council Member Zhuang for her leadership.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks Supports Intro 684 on Gifted and Talented Access

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Temporary Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Today I'm proud to vote.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I think the proper phase is majority leader and temporary.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: There we go.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Today, proud to vote in support of Introduction 684.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to first of all thank Council Member Susan Zwong for her leadership on this particular bill.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Intro 684 would examine how language barriers and geographic location affects access to early elementary gifted and talented programs.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Too many families struggle to find the right programs and understand the process or to secure the services their children are entitled to receive.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: A family should not need money or connections or advanced understanding of the school system to obtain a quality education for their child.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: This bill will help us identify where disparities exist and recommend practical ways to address them.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Again, I encourage my colleagues to vote in favor of this particular bill.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And again, thank you so much for your leadership, Councilmember Swann.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Now we have Councilmember Lee, followed by Councilmember Vernikoff.

chapters.summary: Lee recognizes a delegation from Gangnam, Korea, including Chairman Min Jae-jin Lee and Representatives Jong-Won Lee and Hee-Ok Yum, and discusses exchange of ideas between cities.
chapters.title: Council Member Lee Welcomes Delegation from Gangnam, Korea

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: I wanted to recognize some special guests that we have here from Korea in the province of Gangnam, which I'm sure you guys know, oppa Gangnam style, right?

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So we have in the back here, we have Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Min Jae-jin Lee, who is almost like the speaker of the city council in Gangnam.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So let's welcome him.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And then we also have Representative Jong-Won Lee, as well as Representative Hee-Ok Yum.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So we just had a meeting right before this to really exchange a lot of ideas on similar issues that we are going through as different cities across the world.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And also to talk about how we can learn more from one another.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And so we are very honored to have them here in the People's House at City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: And hopefully we will be able to visit them, Deputy Speaker, on that delegation trip we've been talking about to Korea as well.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: So thank you so much for being here and making the long trip to City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Linda Lee
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember, and welcome to our students and to our delegation from Korea.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: It's very nice to have you here.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Now, next up is Councilmember Vernikoff.

chapters.summary: Vernikov explains Intro 489A, which creates a centralized online database for towed vehicles and an opt-in notification system, thanking colleagues and agencies for their work.
chapters.title: Council Member Vernikov Advocates for Intro 489A on Towing Database

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Thank you, Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: I am beyond thrilled to see Introduction 489A, which will create a modern, streamlined, and centralized towing database passing today.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Intro 489A will create a centralized online database allowing New Yorkers to search for information on any vehicle that has been moved or towed from public or private property by a city entity or licensed private tow operator.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: This will replace an outdated and non-functional system that has frustrated many vehicle owners.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Most towers do not share towed vehicle information with each other and there is no single database where the information is kept, so owners are currently in a scramble to locate their towed or moved vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov
utterances.text: Once this portal is created, the public will be able to utilize one centralized portal that will greatly limit frustration, save them time, hassle, and perhaps some money.

utterances.speaker: Inna Vernikov

chapters.summary: Aldebol speaks in support of Resolution 458A, designating Little Yemen in the East Bronx as an official New York State cultural district, highlighting the Yemeni community's contributions and the need to combat Islamophobia.
chapters.title: Council Member Aldebol Advocates for Little Yemen Cultural District

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you, Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Buenos dias.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Today we'll be voting on Resolution 0458A, supporting the designation of Little Yemen, a neighborhood in Van Ness, Morris Park, as an official New York State cultural district.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: By passing this resolution, we can affirm our support for the Yemeni community and our united stance against Islamophobia, xenophobia, and racism.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Little Yemen is a vibrant community with a proud history that I have the honor of

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: representing on city council.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Its cultural institutions, community organizations, small businesses, and residents are an important part of the East Bronx's identity.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: The cultural district designation would not only recognize and celebrate the Yemeni community's rich cultural heritage and contributions to the East Bronx, it will provide new funding pathways for investment into the community.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: For generations, our neighborhoods in the East Bronx have been shaped by new people moving here from across the city, the country, and around the world.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Each new wave has brought their own culture and traditions to the area while also integrating with the existing communities and becoming true Bronxites in their own right.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: This beautiful history has created a unique mix of food, languages, religions, arts, and culture that make our corner of the East Bronx and the Bronx more widely so special.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: And little Yemen is a perfect example of this.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: I'd like to thank my colleague, Senator Fernandez, and Assemblymember Zacarro for championing this legislation in Albany.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you, Speaker Menon and Deputy Speaker.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you for your support.

utterances.speaker: Shirley Aldebol
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Louis speaks about the crisis of uterine fibroids affecting Black women, urging support for Intro 1113 (provider training) and Intro 1114 (annual reporting on cervical and ovarian cancer screenings).
chapters.title: Council Member Louis Urges Support for Black Women's Reproductive Health Bills

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I need to say something that doesn't get often said.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Being a black woman in America is an act of endurance.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Every single day we navigate a world that was not designed with us in mind, a healthcare system that has historically diminished our pain, minimized our concerns, and

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: delivered us as subpar care.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We walk into doctors'offices and have to fight to be heard, and we are dying at rates that should shock and shock the conscience of every person in this chamber.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: So we have to fight.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We have to legislate, and we have to demand that the health care system that is supposed to serve us actually does.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: One of the most significant and most overlooked crises in black women's reproductive health has been uterine fibroids.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Studies show that more than 80% of black women will develop fibroids by the age of 50.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Black women experience a nearly three-fold higher incidence rate and are more likely to undergo surgery, and fibroids remain the leading cause of hysterectomies in the United States, many of which may be preventable with earlier diagnosis and better options.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Intro 1113 would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to develop mandatory training for health care providers on the diagnosis and treatment of uterine fibroids, and Intro 1114 would require the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: to report annually on cervical and ovarian cancer screenings and diagnosis across New York City.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Together, these bills demand better data and better care because black women deserve it.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support both intros.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilmember Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Councilmember Banks, followed by Councilmember Wilson.

chapters.summary: Banks recognizes Youth Empowerment Month, welcomes students from PAT High School in his district, and thanks educators and mentors.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks Recognizes Youth Empowerment Month and Students

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to first recognize the Deputy Leader Speaker, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Natasha Williams, for sponsoring the Resolution 193 back in 2024, which I was proud to co-sponsor, which designated October as Youth Empowerment Month here in the City of New York.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And in that spirit, I also want to take the opportunity and time to welcome the young people and educators and mentors and community organizations who joined us today at City Hall.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: I want to thank you for your work and all the work that you've done to educate and encourage and empower young people across the city.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: A special shout out goes to the students from Pat High School in my district.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And also I want to thank you for coming to City Hall and participating in the civic process and representing the 42nd Council District.

chapters.summary: Banks offers condolences on the passing of Calypso legend Mighty Sparrow, noting his impact on Trinidadian and Caribbean communities.
chapters.title: Council Member Banks Honors Mighty Sparrow

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: And also, with the remainder of my time, I want to take this time to give condolences and recognition to the mighty, mighty Sparrow.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: In his recent passing, we know him as the slinger Francesco, at the current Trinidadian serving the New York City Council.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: It was a major loss that hit especially close to home.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Like some, many Trinidadians and to Bogonians, members of the Caribbean community who grew up to Mighty Sparrow's music all around me, family, friends, gatherings.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: We know how important his life was to Calypso, especially in the Caribbean and here throughout the United States.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: So again, our condolences to his family and to all the Caribbeans here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Chris Banks
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Councilmember Wilson, followed by Councilmember Santuoso.

chapters.summary: Wilson introduces Intro 1130, requiring AI model advertisements to disclose independent safety validation and prohibiting false safety claims, citing concerns from the AI hearing.
chapters.title: Council Member Wilson Introduces Intro 1130 on AI Advertising Transparency

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you to the Honorable Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The bill I'm formally introducing today, Intro 1130, pushes for more transparency, accuracy, and accountability in AI advertising.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: It requires that advertisements for AI models disclose whether they've undergone independent safety validation.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: The bill also prohibits false or misleading statements regarding the safety of an AI model in advertisements.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: This is a common-sense bill that will keep consumers informed and AI companies honest.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I believe that breakthroughs in AI technology show real promise, for example, in medical or scientific research.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: But we need to ensure that the pace of innovation does not leave average New Yorkers behind and that this technology's potential excesses are kept in check.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I was concerned in the hearing earlier this week when representatives from top AI companies could not clearly gauge the risk of a cataclysmic event caused by their technology.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: did not know whether they had insurance coverage for such an event and could not name who at these companies would be in charge of responding to a potential AI-related cataclysm, and whether employees who have raised safety concerns are being properly protected and heated.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I'm proud to be collaborating with my colleagues on a world-leading endeavor to establish responsible guardrails on AI technology and advertising, and I thank Speaker Menden for her leadership on this issue.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shekar Krishnan
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Santos-Wosso, followed by Councilmember Joseph.

chapters.summary: Santosuosso shares the story of her constituent Connor, a child with Down syndrome, to mark Down Syndrome Awareness Month and advocate for early support services.
chapters.title: Council Member Santosuosso Highlights Down Syndrome Awareness Month

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader, for a day.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: October is Down Syndrome Awareness Month, and so I wanted to take my time today to highlight a very special constituent of mine in Bay Ridge, Connor.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Connor was born a year and a half ago with a congenital heart defect and Down syndrome.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: After an open heart surgery at just four months old, Connor has been doing eight sessions a week of physical therapy, occupational therapy, and speech therapy.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And with the deep love and support of his family and friends, I'm happy to say that Connor is thriving today.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: He has said his first words, has a strong bond with his family, and we are all optimistic.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: for his future.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Children with Down syndrome deserve our support to lead full and dignified lives.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: There are many deep misconceptions about Down syndrome, but Connor's story highlights how we can improve long-term outcomes by starting the work early.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Every kid should have access to the support services that have allowed Connor to overcome so much.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: And I'm eager to spend the rest of my time on the council working with my colleagues to improve things for all of those impacted by Down syndrome.

utterances.speaker: Kayla Santosuosso
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Joseph, followed by Councilmember Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

chapters.summary: Joseph introduces Intro 1111, requiring the NYC Public Schools to report quarterly on Medicaid reimbursement for services to students with disabilities, to ensure transparency and recover funds.
chapters.title: Council Member Joseph Introduces Intro 1111 on Medicaid Reimbursement for School Services

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I am glad to introduce Intro 1111.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Every year, our school provides speech therapy, occupational therapy, counseling, nursing, and transportation to thousands of students with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Many of those services qualify for Medicaid reimbursement, federal and state dollars that belong in our classroom.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: But right now, we cannot answer a simple question.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: How much of that money are we collecting, and how much are we leaving on the table?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: This bill requires the New York City Public School to report quarterly by borough and by district on how many services were delivered, how many were claimed, how many were reimbursed,

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: and where the gaps are, whether it's missing paperwork, consent forms, or missed deadlines.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It'll also ask a question families have been asking for years.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Are students receiving the services their IEPs require?

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Every dollar we recover is a dollar for our kids.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Right now, hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers are at risk of losing Medicaid eligibility.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Making these dollars...

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: is that much more critical.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Far too many students with disabilities fall through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Transparency is how we fix this pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Also, thank you.

chapters.summary: Joseph adds the Haitian community's voice to the farewell for Mighty Sparrow, recalling his 2004 Carnegie Hall performance celebrating Haiti's bicentennial and his role in Caribbean unity.
chapters.title: Council Member Joseph Honors Mighty Sparrow

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Today I want to honor a giant.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Dr.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Slinger Francisco Mighty Sparrow, the Calypso King of the world, passed away here in New York on September 27 at the age of 91.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Today I'm adding the voice of the Haitian community to the world's farewell.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: For more than seven decades, Sparrow sang the joys he never struggled, the struggles and the truth of the Caribbean people.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And he never forgot that Haiti is where Caribbean freedom began.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In January of 2004, when Haiti marked 200 years of independence, Sparrow took the stage at Carnegie Hall right here in New York City to celebrate the world's first free black republic.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: He honored our ancestors, our revolution, and our pride.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: He was not Haitian by birth, but he was family.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: He saw us, he stood with us, and he reminded the whole Caribbean that we are one people.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: To his family and to the people of Trinidad and Tobago and Grenada, our hearts are with you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: From Flatbush to Port-au-Prince, merci Sparrow.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Reposez en paix.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Shulman, followed by Councilmember Maloney.

chapters.summary: Schulman introduces Intro 1124, requiring food protection course certifications to be renewed every five years to ensure food service managers have up-to-date knowledge.
chapters.title: Council Member Schulman Introduces Intro 1124 on Food Protection Certification Renewal

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you, Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Today I am introducing Intro 1124, legislation that would require food protection course certifications to be renewed every five years.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Food safety is a fundamental part of protecting the health of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Everyday food service workers across our city are responsible for preparing and handling food that is consumed by

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: They play an essential role in preventing foodborne illness and ensuring that food is prepared and stored safely.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Currently, once a person completes the required food protection course and passes the exam, the certification does not need to be renewed on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: But food safety practices, regulations, and public health guidance can evolve over time.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This legislation would establish a five-year renewal requirement, giving food service managers an opportunity to refresh their knowledge of safe food handling, proper storage,

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: and temperature control, preventing cross-contamination, allergen awareness, sanitation, and other important food protection practices.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: This is a straightforward, common-sense step to make sure that the people responsible for managing food service establishments have up-to-date knowledge and training.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to sign on to this legislation and help continue strengthening food safety protections for all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: A couple of things I want to point out.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: One, this is the second piece of legislation that was...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Where I got the idea from my chief of staff, who now has two pieces of legislation that he has helped me with.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And I believe that we're only as good as our staff members, so this is really important to me.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And the other thing I want to point out is that food certification,

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: licenses are renewed in other states.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Here is, we're the only city, or one of the only cities that doesn't do that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We give it once and that's it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I urge my colleagues to sign on and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Maloney.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: All by Councilmember Riley.

chapters.summary: Maloney introduces Intro 1115, giving New Yorkers a path to court when AI companies fail to put reasonable safeguards against foreseeable third-party misuse.
chapters.title: Council Member Maloney Introduces Intro 1115 on AI Liability

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you, Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: First, I want to thank the speaker for her leadership on the most consequential technological shifts of our lifetime with artificial intelligence.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I spent nearly a decade working in technology and building products, and I firmly believe that those with the power to build those technologies also have the responsibility to take reasonable steps to protect the public.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: My bill, 1115, would give New Yorkers a path to court when foreseeable third-party misuse causes harm and an AI company failed to put reasonable safeguards in place.

chapters.summary: Maloney introduces a bill to install sound meters near seaplane bases and publicly report noise data, responding to constituent complaints about seaplane noise along the East River.
chapters.title: Council Member Maloney Introduces Bill on Seaplane Noise Monitoring

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Second, I'm introducing legislation responding to years of constituent quality of life complaints about seaplane noise along the East River.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Right now, we lack consistent public data on how loud and frequent that noise is.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: My bill would install sound meters near active seaplane bases and publicly report on what they detect.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: If New Yorkers are telling us that something is disrupting their daily lives, government should be able to measure it, understand it, and act on the facts.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: I hope my colleagues will join me in supporting both of these bills.

utterances.speaker: Virginia Maloney
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Riley introduces Intro 1121, establishing a program to support justice-involved youth ages 13-24 transitioning from custody to education, employment, or vocational training.
chapters.title: Council Member Riley Introduces Intro 1121 on Reentry for Justice-Involved Youth

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Riley, followed by Councilmember Farias.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you, Acting Majority Leader.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Today I'm proud to introduce three pieces of legislation focused on expanding opportunity, strengthening our city's workforce, and protecting New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: First, Intro 1121 will establish a program to support justice-involved and system-involved young people ages 13 to 24 transitioning from custody into education, employment, vocational training, or apprenticeship.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: The program will help young people secure necessary documents, complete applications, and connect to opportunities with best efforts to begin that work before they leave custody.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Successful reentry starts with a real pathway forward, and I want to thank my former fellow, Shahani, for coming up with this legislation, and welcome my new fellow, Colleen, to the team, and looking forward to your work that we're going to see soon.

chapters.summary: Riley introduces Intro 1122, directing DCAS to assess and strengthen Employee Resource Groups across city government.
chapters.title: Council Member Riley Introduces Intro 1122 on Employee Resource Groups

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Second, Intro 1122 will strengthen access to the Employee Resource Group, also known as ERG, across city government

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: by directing DCAS to assess existing groups, identifying best practices, and providing clear guidance for employees looking to build community and access resources.

chapters.summary: Riley introduces Intro 1123, strengthening whistleblower protections for city employees who report AI-related conduct posing risks to public health or safety.
chapters.title: Council Member Riley Introduces Intro 1123 on Whistleblower Protection for AI Risks

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: And finally, Intro 1123 strengthens our city's whistleblower protection by protecting employees who report AI-related conduct

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: they reasonably believe possess a substantial and specific risk to public health or safety.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: I want to thank Speaker Mendez's leadership and my colleagues who are here at the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: As technology advances, our responsibility is to protect New Yorkers, and we must advance with it.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Colleagues, I respectfully...

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: ask you to support and sign on to these three bills as we work to ensure our city's government is responsive to the needs of New Yorkers today and prepare for challenges tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Kevin C. Riley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Farias, followed by Councilmember Brewer.

chapters.summary: Farias introduces Intro 1106, requiring the NYPD to expand annual domestic violence reporting with detailed breakdowns by demographics, geography, and language, while protecting survivor identities.
chapters.title: Council Member Farias Introduces Intro 1106 on Domestic Violence Reporting

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Today I'm introducing Intro 1106 requiring the NYPD to expand its annual domestic violence reporting to include the total number of domestic violence arrests and a more detailed breakdown of domestic violence incidences.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This builds on my extensive work alongside coalition partners to strengthen survivor protections.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I especially want to thank and recognize VOA New York, whose expertise and guidance have helped me shape much of this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: As chair of the Committee on Women and Gender Equity, I want this council to be able to follow what happens when a survivor reaches out for help.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: A survivor may call 911, walk into a precinct, or encounter an officer responding to another incident.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: They may need an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: They may be reporting abuse for the first time after years of threats.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Our oversight must account for those experiences.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: My bill would require domestic incident report data broken down by age, gender, ethnicity, race, language spoken, and geography, including council district and precinct, as well as how the individual came into contact with the department.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: It expressly requires the NYPD to protect the identities of people named in those reports.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: With this information, we can better examine who our response is reaching, where language access and outreach need greater attention,

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: and how we direct resources to communities seeking help.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Survivors take an enormous risk when they report abuse, and this council has a responsibility to scrutinize the response they receive and press for improvements that make seeking help safer and more accessible.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to join me in supporting this legislation by signing on as a co-sponsor.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: David M. Carr
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer, followed by Councilmember Marano.

chapters.summary: Brewer introduces three interns and announces the upcoming invitation-only service for Gloria Steinem.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer Recognizes Interns and Notes Gloria Steinem Service

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I have three wonderful interns here today.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Modu Dikan, who is from Mercy University.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Katie Bay, who is a grad student at Hunter College Social Work, Silverman School.
